main_text.p: poris animati,ceu natura, quæ principium eft & caufa motus rei naturalis,uelut often dit Philofophus libro, Phyficorum fecun-Cap.I.do. Deinde animalia, quæ imaginatione pollent, etiamfi cœca concipiant, marem nec uidere, neque imaginari queunt: tunc enim uel impeditæ funt animales facultates, uel adeo languidæ,ut penè nihil, aut debelissime quicquam moliri posint:Hu-iusmodi sunt equæ & canes, quæ tamen pullos & catulos marib.similes procreant. His accedunt aves, quarum mares maribus,& fœminæ fœminis similes producunt.

Quod certè nunquam fieret,si quid in ipsis mutaret imaginatio. Quare similitudo partus ad parentes, aut ad alios quosuis non imaginationi matris referenda est, sed formatrici facultati, quæ è femine iam concepto in embryonem transfertur,& ab hoc in animal perfectum. Etenim hanc vim suo femini indit pater, & hoc fœtui: quoniam patris calor à feminis calore specie nō dif-fert, sed duntaxat numero. Propterea
per eum in utero ipse pater generat suæ speciei fœtum.

page.notes: Printed text, marginal "Cap.I." and "T 2" signature read; the catchword "EXER-" is at the foot. Word "posint" in the printed line read as "pofsint" (possibly "posint"); "debelissime" is printed "debelisime" with a long-s-like form, given here as printed. Spelling "Hu-iusmodi" splits across a line end. Some letters at the line ends and in "pofsint" are doubtful and should be checked.
